description: Chlorine has been going down every day. I thought it was the old batch so I made a new one Wednesday, but it kept dropping. 0.18 this morning.

expected.diagnosis: Slow chlorine drift that a fresh batch didn't fix — likely a worn pump diaphragm or check valve. It has now crossed below the 0.2 mg/L EPA minimum.
key_steps: Switch to the standby feed pump and contact the RMW now (Manual 3.3, 8.1)
Inspect the pump diaphragm and check valve (Manual 3.5)
If not back to 0.2 mg/L within 4 hours, notify ADEC and prepare for a boil-water notice (Manual 3.3, 8.2)

description: Just doing my weekly review. Readings look normal to me. Anything I should be doing?

expected.diagnosis: Normal operation. All readings are within target ranges with no trends.
key_steps: Keep taking daily entry-point readings by 9:00 AM (Manual 1.2)
Backwash on schedule at 0.25 NTU, 8 psi, or 72 hours (Manual 2.2)
Swap duty filters weekly (Manual 2.1)

description: The duty circulation pump tripped again last night and the loop return temp dropped to 38°F. I switched to the standby pump and reset the breaker on the duty pump. It's -15°F out.

expected.diagnosis: Duty circulation pump is repeatedly tripping its breaker — the 4th time in about 3 weeks, likely a failing motor. Each event was fixed, but the recurrence in winter risks a freeze-up.
key_steps: Run on the standby circulation pump and leave the duty pump breaker off (Manual 7.2, 6.2)
Contact the RMW — the same problem has happened 3 or more times in 30 days (Manual 8.1)
Check loop return temperature every shift (Manual 6.1)

description: pH has slipped down a bit each day this week, 6.7 now. The soda ash day tank is nearly empty and the last batch looked thin.

expected.diagnosis: Soda ash batch was weak and is running out, so pH is drifting down. It's below 6.8 but still above the 6.5 limit.
key_steps: Refill the soda ash day tank and check the feed pump is primed (Manual 5.2, 7.3)
Raise the soda ash pump stroke in 5% steps and retest after 1 hour (Manual 5.2)
Calibrate the pH meter to confirm (Manual 5.1)

description: Power went out for about 3 hours last night. When it came back I restarted everything. This morning filtered turbidity is 1.4 on both meters.

expected.diagnosis: Filters were restarted after the power outage without filter-to-waste, sending a turbidity spike to the clearwell. Filtered turbidity is above the 1.0 NTU EPA limit.
key_steps: Contact the RMW immediately and ADEC within 24 hours (Manual 4.3, 8.1)
Restart filters with filter-to-waste before sending water to the clearwell (Manual 7.5, 2.3)
Prepare for a boil-water notice since turbidity is above 1.0 NTU (Manual 8.2, 8.3)

description: Loop return temp was 39°F this morning. The boiler had a fault light on. I reset it and the temp is coming back up. Circ pump was running fine.

expected.diagnosis: Boiler fault reduced heat-add to the circulating loop. The reset restored heating, and circulation was never lost.
key_steps: Recheck loop return temperature after 1 hour (Manual 6.2)
Check heat-add settings (Manual 6.2)
Log the boiler fault (Manual 1.3)

description: New operator mixed the hypochlorite batch yesterday. Chlorine went from 1.1 to 1.9 overnight.

expected.diagnosis: New hypochlorite batch was probably mixed too strong. Residual is high but under 2.0 mg/L, so watch it closely.
key_steps: Check the batch was mixed correctly: 1 gallon of 12.5% hypochlorite filled to the 20-gallon mark (Manual 3.2, 3.4)
If it rises above 2.0 mg/L, lower the pump stroke in 5% steps and retest after 30 minutes (Manual 3.4)
Log the batch and readings (Manual 1.3)

description: A water main broke by the school this morning. The gauge near there shows 15 psi. Plant readings were normal.

expected.diagnosis: Main break near the school has dropped pressure below 20 psi, allowing possible contamination. Treated water quality at the plant is fine.
key_steps: Contact the RMW and ADEC now — pressure below 20 psi and a main break (Manual 7.4, 8.1)
Issue a boil-water notice for the affected area; if you can't reach the RMW or ADEC within 2 hours, issue a precautionary notice (Manual 8.2, 8.3)
Post the notice at the washeteria, school, clinic, store, and post office and announce it on VHF (Manual 8.3)

description: Soda ash pump lost prime again — pH dropped to 6.9. Same thing happened about 10 days ago. I bled the air and it's feeding again.

expected.diagnosis: Soda ash feed pump losing prime again, likely worn check valves or crystals in the suction line. Two occurrences, not yet 3 in 30 days, and pH is still above 6.5.
key_steps: Prime lost again within about 10 days: replace the check valves with the spare kit (Manual 7.3)
Check the foot valve and suction line for crystals or air leaks (Manual 7.3)
Retest pH after 1 hour (Manual 5.2)

description: Turbidity crept up through the week, 0.29 now. Filter has been on since last Monday — about 70 hours. pH and chlorine are fine.

expected.diagnosis: End of a normal filter run — turbidity passed the 0.25 NTU trigger near 72 hours of run time. The backwash is overdue.
key_steps: Backwash now — turbidity passed 0.25 NTU and the run is near 72 hours (Manual 2.2)
Backwash 10–15 minutes, then filter-to-waste until below 0.15 NTU (Manual 2.3)
Confirm with the bench meter and recheck at 1 and 4 hours (Manual 4.4, 2.4)
